title: Lookup picker
summary: A select-style field for a long list (customers, products, users) that does not fit pk-combobox: its popup holds a searchable, pageable pk-data-table, so the reader tells rows apart by columns. Set the load(query) callback as a property, exactly as pk-data-table's: it receives { page, pageSize, sort, sortDir, search, filters } and { signal }, and returns (or resolves to) { rows, total }; loading, error and empty states come from the table. Picking a row sets value to its rowKey field and closes the popup. The field shows the option's label: its labelKey field when picked in this session, else selectedLabels[value], else what the resolve(keys) callback property returns for it ({ key: label } or [{ key, label }]), so a stored value shows its name even when its row is on no loaded page. The popup is built on the first open: a closed picker loads nothing but itself.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several rows can be chosen: the popup table gets a checkbox column (the selection survives paging and searching; there is no select-all across pages) and stays open while ticking; the chosen rows show as removable chips under the field. The form submits one entry per key under name.

props.name: values
props.description: The keys of the chosen rows when multiple is set, as an array of strings (any text, commas included); what the form submits. A form reset sets it back to its initial value silently. Chip labels come from the rows seen, selectedLabels or resolve(keys), which is asked once for all keys with no label.

props.name: max
props.description: The most rows a multiple picker accepts (0: no limit). A tick past it is undone and announced.

props.name: value
props.description: The key (rowKey field) of the chosen row; what the form submits. A form reset sets it back to its initial value silently, as a native control does.

props.name: config
props.description: The popup table's config, as pk-data-table's: { columns, filters?, empty?, noResults?, loadError?, pageSize?, pageSizeOptions?, sort?, sortDir?, searchable?, searchLabel?, searchDebounce?, pagerLabel? }. columns is required for the table to show anything.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: The row field that identifies a row: what value holds.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: The row field shown in the field once a row is picked (the rowKey field when the row has none).

props.name: selectedLabels
props.description: { key: label } for values whose row is not on a loaded page, so the field can show a stored value's name without asking the server.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the field and of the popup. pk-field fills it from its own label when this is empty.

props.name: description
props.description: Help and error text, exposed as aria-description; pk-field fills it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Blocks interaction; also set by a disabled fieldset.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shows the value but cannot open the popup.

props.name: required
props.description: The form cannot be submitted while no row is chosen.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Shows the invalid state and sets aria-invalid; set by pk-field or pk-form (or by a Blazor EditContext).

events.name: input
events.description: The value changed (native, composed). Read event.target.value.

events.name: change
events.description: The reader picked a row (native, composed).

events.name: pk-lookup-select
events.description: A row was picked: its key, its label and the row object from load().

events.name: pk-values-change
events.description: The multiple selection changed (a row ticked or unticked, a chip removed): the keys and their labels. input and change are raised with it.

events.name: pk-lookup-toggle
events.description: The popup opened or closed by itself (a click, a key, a pick, Escape, an outside press, focus leaving); open already has the new value. Not raised for a change the host made.

parts.name: popover
parts.description: The pk-popover that holds the popup (placement, outside press, Escape and focus return are its).

parts.name: control
parts.description: The pk-button that shows the chosen label (or the placeholder) and opens the popup.

parts.name: chips
parts.description: The list of chips (pk-tag, removable) under a multiple picker.

parts.name: table
parts.description: The pk-data-table in the popup, created on the first open.

parts.name: status
parts.description: The polite live region that announces loading and the result count.

a11y: The field is a real button (pk-button) that the popover marks aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded, named "<label>: <chosen label or placeholder>"; the popup is a labelled dialog holding the table's search box and rows, so focus really moves into it (a combobox with aria-activedescendant cannot reach rows inside the table's shadow roots; this is the disclosure-plus-dialog pattern, not role=combobox). Down or Up on the field, Enter or Space open it and focus lands in the search box; Down there enters the rows, Up, Down, Home and End walk them, Enter or Space picks the focused row and closes; Escape closes and returns focus to the field; Tab moves on through the pager and out of the picker, which closes it. A polite status announces loading and the number of results. The table's own loading, error and empty states keep their roles. The field and the rows are at least 44px tall on a phone. Multiple: the chips are a labelled list (role=list, each pk-tag role=listitem) whose remove buttons are real buttons (named "Remove" by pk-tag: the chip text is the context); removing one returns focus to the field and a status announces it. The table rows have checkboxes named for their row, and a tick past max is undone with "Limit of N reached" announced.

examples.title: Customer lookup (set load from script: an inline script cannot run under this site's CSP)
Several customers (chips; labels for keys that are not on a loaded page come from selected-labels)
examples.html: <pk-lookup-picker multiple label="Customers" placeholder="Choose customers" values='["C1","C2","C3"]' selected-labels='{"C1":"Acme Hardware","C2":"Globex","C3":"Initech"}' config='{"columns":[{"key":"name","label":"Name"}]}'></pk-lookup-picker>

writes.why: The picker creates the table in its own shadow tree on the first open and drives it (rows clickable or, for multiple, selectable with page-only selection; keyed; its config and a wrapped load). Only clickable and selected are writes the check can see; selected follows values.

writes.target: the text span of the field
writes.why: Marks the text span (created by the picker in its own shadow tree) while it shows the placeholder, so it is styled muted.
